## My Reasoning

I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life, just like my father did. The soil here is flat and irrigated — it used to be salty alkali ground but it's workable now. I have 10 mu of fields.

There's no question what I'll grow: **winter wheat and summer corn**. That's the rotation here. Everyone does it. Wheat goes in around the 10th to 20th of October, you harvest it in June, then you get corn in before July and pull it in September. Two crops, same land, every year. I've done this for 30 years.

For wheat, I'll buy improved seeds from the county seed station — Kenong 199 or Jimai 22, whichever they have. Good yield, I know how they behave. After I pull the corn in late September, I'll run the rotary tiller over the field to chop up the stalks and loosen things up, then broadcast compound fertilizer and sow. I water three times: November to protect roots before the cold comes in, April when the wheat joints, and once more before heading in May. I'll spray herbicide in early spring and one pass of fungicide before harvest — rust gets bad some years.

For corn after the wheat comes off, I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — reliable, good ears. I don't plow before planting corn, no time and the ground is still okay. I drill it straight into the stubble. Lay down fertilizer at planting, top-dress urea when it's knee-high. Water once or twice if the summer rains are short. Spray once for borer, maybe once more if the aphids show up.

I don't experiment. These inputs and varieties are what my neighbors use, what the township agronomist says, and what I know from experience. I'm not changing at 58.
